items.title: What Dunning and Kruger actually showed
items.claim: Dunning and Kruger (1999) reported a finding that became internet shorthand. Their actual graph showed something subtler. Which is closest?

options.text: The least competent rated themselves below average
Most people overestimated their performance; the lowest performers overestimated the most
The most competent thought they were the worst

items.reveal_title: Most people overestimated; the least competent overestimated most
items.reveal:
In the original study, participants in the bottom quartile of test performance rated themselves around the 62nd percentile.

Statisticians (Nuhfer et al., 2017) have argued part of the effect is regression to the mean rather than pure metacognitive failure.
items.why: Popular versions of findings often lose the nuance that makes them scientifically interesting.

items.title: Growth mindset meta-analyses
items.claim: Carol Dweck's growth mindset theory inspired large-scale school interventions. What did Sisk et al.'s 2018 meta-analysis report about the effect on academic achievement?

options.text: Very large positive effects in all settings
Small effects on average, larger for at-risk students

items.reveal:
Sisk et al. (2018) found a weak overall correlation between mindset and achievement, with stronger effects among lower-attaining and at-risk groups.

A 2019 US national experiment (Yeager et al.) found small but real gains for lower-achieving high schoolers.
items.why: Educational interventions rarely produce uniform effects across populations.

items.title: The multi-store model was too simple for working memory
items.claim: Atkinson and Shiffrin's 1968 multi-store model split memory into sensory, short-term and long-term stores. What replaced its account of short-term memory?

options.text: Nothing — the multi-store model is unchanged

Baddeley and Hitch's 1974 working memory model — a central executive coordinating a phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad and (later) episodic buffer — better fitted evidence that STM is not a single unitary store

items.reveal:
Patients with impaired STM (e.g., KF, studied by Shallice and Warrington 1970) could nonetheless retain visual information and form new long-term memories — evidence STM had components. Baddeley and Hitch (1974) proposed a multi-component working memory. The episodic buffer was added by Baddeley in 2000.

The multi-store model is still taught as a stepping stone but is superseded for STM specifically.
items.why: Models that fit the original data often fail later, more specific data. Working memory's multiple components matter for education, clinical assessment and cognitive neuroscience.
